steps.title: What a FRET line tells you
steps.text:
A static species sits on its static line in the E–τ_F plot. A molecule exchanging between two states within the burst bows towards longer lifetimes, onto a dynamic line. We will draw one of each.

The tool starts with one FD (Gaussian) component, which is what the static line needs.

steps.title: Step 1 — choose what varies
steps.text:
Open Sweep. Set Vary to C0 … · RDA0, the mean distance, with Min 20 and Max 120 Å. Set τ_D0 to your donor-only lifetime (4 ns if you have none).

The Gaussian width w in the Editor is the linker width, which bends the line away from the diagonal. 6 Å is typical.

steps.title: Step 2 — compute the static line
steps.text: Press + Add FRET line. The orange curve is the static line. At τ_F = 2 ns it sits near E = 0.56, while the diagonal 1 − τ_F/τ_D0 gives 0.50.

steps.title: Step 3 — a second state
steps.text: On Components, press + Add for a second FD (Gaussian). In the Editor, set component C0's R_DA to one state (e.g. 40 Å) and C1's to the other (70 Å).

steps.title: Step 4 — sweep the fraction
steps.text: Back on Sweep, set Vary to fraction · C0, Min 0 and Max 1, then press + Add FRET line again. The new curve joins the static line at both states and bows out between them. A population in that gap exchanges within the burst.

steps.title: Use the lines
steps.text: Save CSV writes every line (τ_F, τ_X, E per point). Push to ndX overlays them on visible ndX overlay panels, over your burst histogram.
